title: Suffixes -s, -es, -ed, -ing
examples: What is the sound for the past tense?
Can you show me how to add -ing?

explain.say: Today we learn about adding endings to words. We are looking at suffixes today. A suffix is a little ending we add to a word.
For making things plural, we often add an 's' sound. For example, one book becomes two books. We add the 's' sound.
If a word ends in 'sh', 'ch', or 's', we add 'es'. For example, one box becomes two boxes. We add the 'es' sound.
For past tense verbs, we often add '-ed'. This makes a /t/ or /d/ sound. For example, walk becomes walked. We add '-ed'.
When we talk about what is happening now, we add '-ing'. For example, play becomes playing. We add '-ing'.
Look at the word 'dog'. If we want more than one dog, we say dogs. We added the 's' sound to the end.

draw.text: Real life: one dog, many dogs

faq.q: When do I use -es instead of just -s?
faq.a: You use -es when the word ends with 'sh', 'ch', or 's'. This makes the ending sound clearer. You might also ask, 'Do I always add -es to words ending in s?' or 'What about plural words ending in s?'
asks: Do I add -es to words like bus?

faq.q: How do I know if a past tense verb needs -ed?
faq.a: Most verbs just need you to add '-ed' to the end. This makes the past action sound. You could also ask, 'What sound does past tense make?' or 'Does every past tense word end in -ed?'
asks: What is the past tense sound?
Do I always say -ed for past tense?

faq.q: Is '-ing' always for actions happening now?
faq.a: Yes, '-ing' usually tells us an action that is happening right now. It shows the action in progress. You might also ask, 'What does -ing mean?' or 'Can I use -ing for something finished?'

faq.q: Do I have to change the spelling when adding these endings?
faq.a: Sometimes you do, especially with the doubling rule. You must listen carefully to the sound at the end of the word. You could ask, 'Do I change the spelling?' or 'Is there a rule for spelling changes?'

faq.q: What is the difference between plurals and past tense?
faq.a: Plurals tell us there is more than one thing. Past tense tells us an action already happened. You could ask, 'Is -s for things or actions?' or 'What is the job of -ed?'

facts: Past tense verbs often end with -ed.
The -ing ending shows an action happening now.
If a word ends in 'sh', 'ch', or 's', use -es for plurals.

quiz.say: One cat becomes two cats. What ending did you add?
quiz.why: You add -s because the word cat is simple.

wrong.0: This ending is mostly for past actions.
wrong.1: This ending shows an action happening now.
wrong.3: This is only for words ending in sh, ch, or s.

quiz.say: The word 'wash' becomes 'washes' for more than one. What is the rule here?

wrong.0: This ending is for past time, not plurals.
wrong.1: This ending shows an action, not a group of things.
wrong.3: You need -es because of the 'sh' sound.

quiz.say: Yesterday, I played. What ending did you add to 'play'?
quiz.why: You add -ed to show that the action already finished.

wrong.1: This ending is for making things more than one.
wrong.2: This ending is for specific sounds like 'sh'.
wrong.3: This ending shows the action happening right now.
